payload.title: How to Get Married in New Zealand as an Australian
payload.excerpt: Yes, you can get married in New Zealand as Australians, and you do not need to be New Zealand citizens: visitors to New Zealand can marry there. What you need is a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry, and a registered celebrant to marry you.
key_takeaways: Australians can marry legally in New Zealand with a marriage licence and a registered celebrant, and neither of you needs to be a New Zealand citizen.
From Australia you apply with the overseas notice of intended marriage form, sign its declaration before an authorised person, and then visit a registry office in New Zealand before the ceremony.
The licence must be in place at least 3 working days before the wedding, lasts 3 months, and only covers the venues you name on it, so name a back-up.
The Copy of Particulars you sign on the day is not a marriage certificate, so order the certificate afterwards and ask any Australian organisation receiving it whether it wants an Apostille.

faq.q: Do we need to be New Zealand residents to marry there?
faq.a: No. You do not need to be a New Zealand citizen, and visitors to New Zealand can marry in New Zealand. Couples who live outside New Zealand apply with the BDM 58 form.

faq.q: How do we get a marriage licence in New Zealand from Australia?
faq.a: Complete the BDM 58 form except for the statutory declaration, sign that declaration before one of the authorised people listed on the form, and send the fee to Births, Deaths and Marriages. Arrange the licence at least 3 working days before the wedding, as it expires after 3 months. When you arrive, visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony.

faq.q: Can we get married in New Zealand without witnesses?
faq.a: No. You need 2 witnesses who understand what is happening, can clearly identify you both and are satisfied you both consent. They must be physically present with you and your celebrant.

faq.q: Is a New Zealand marriage legal in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law, though you cannot register it in Australia. Australia is an Apostille country for New Zealand documents, so ask the organisation receiving your certificate whether it wants one.

faq.q: Can we elope in a national park in New Zealand?
faq.a: Ask your celebrant and the [Department of Conservation](https://www.doc.govt.nz/) before you choose the spot, including whether permission is needed and who applies for it. Whatever you decide, the location goes on your licence application with a back-up venue.
